title: When successful requests return bad data
scenario: Customers sometimes see strange delivery days or shipping prices. Sometimes the values are missing. The graphs still say the requests worked. Find out why.
why: Getting a reply does not mean the reply is right. Stop the shop from showing impossible values, while keeping stock information available.
reproduce: First record normal stock, delivery days and shipping price. Predict what might go wrong. In Network Faults, choose Primary Shipping and Wrong or missing values, then click Apply response fault. Refresh shipping a few times. Leave the fault on while you try a fix.
assignment: Can you hide wrong shipping information while keeping stock visible?

fields.label: Normal results and prediction
fields.prompt: Record stock, delivery days and shipping price before the fault. What do you expect to change?

fields.label: What you saw
fields.prompt: Record strange numbers or blanks from a few refreshes. What do the request and response-check graphs show?

fields.label: Your explanation
fields.prompt: Why can a request work but the information still be wrong? What else could explain it?

fields.label: Your change and why it helps
fields.prompt: Which setting did you change? Why would waiting less or pausing requests not fix wrong values?

fields.label: Check the result
fields.prompt: Leave the fault on. Are wrong values hidden? Does stock still appear? Does Grafana show blocked values?

fields.label: Finish and reset
fields.prompt: What improved? What is still missing? Remove the fault, restore defaults and check normal shipping returns.

solution: The main delivery company replies, but sometimes sends negative delivery days, a negative price or empty fields. Other replies are normal. Stock still works.
The requests count as successful because a reply arrived. Response checks in Grafana separately shows wrong or missing values.
Under Shipping, select Check response data and click Apply Shipping settings. Wrong shipping information becomes unavailable. Normal shipping values and stock still appear.
The checker hides bad values. It does not fix the delivery company or call the backup. Remove the response fault and restore defaults to finish.

text.hints_description: Open one at a time if you get stuck.

hints.title: Hint 1 · Look at the shop
hints.explanation: Refresh shipping a few times. Are the stock count, delivery days and price sensible? Write down any strange numbers or blanks.

hints.title: Hint 2 · Compare the graphs
hints.explanation: A successful request only means that a reply arrived. It can still contain wrong values. Look at Response checks in Grafana. The graph takes about a minute to show a new pattern clearly.

hints.title: Hint 3 · Try a response check
hints.explanation: A timeout stops waiting. A breaker pauses failed requests. Neither checks the values in a reply. Under Shipping, select Check response data and click Apply Shipping settings. Wrong values should disappear; stock should stay visible.
